result:
I found and fixed 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 06, 143 | The cap was applied to the price before the discount was calculated: `min(base, cap) * pct` | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 15 | Used 9% instead of the documented 8% | Changed to 8% |
| 17, 70, 150 | The 10,000 won cap only applied once the discount went over 20,000 | Always cap the discount |
| 69 | The 50,000 won cap only applied once the discount went over 100,000 | Always cap the discount |
| 63 | Threshold was `>= 13`, but the docstring says 12+ units | Changed to `>= 12` |
| 64 | Threshold was `>= 21`, but the docstring says 20+ units | Changed to `>= 20` |
| 82 | Used `round()`, which breaks the "floor to the won" rule | Changed to `// 100` |

**Verification:** I wrote a script that reads each of the 150 docstrings and compares the function's output against a reference calculation over boundary values. After the fixes it reports no mismatches.

The script missed rule 150 at first because none of its test inputs hit the in-between discount range. I found that one by reading the code. Rules 150 and 17 now give the correct capped amounts in a separate spot check.

Rule 141 is written differently from the others (`qty > 10` instead of `>= 10`), but it always gives the same result, so I left it alone.

STATUS: DONE
